sample.title: Thumb pulse, finger backbeat
sample.summary: Keep quarter notes under the thumb while index and middle answer on beats 2 and 4.
sample.description: [What it is] Keeping quarter-note bass under the thumb while the index and middle play answers on beats 2 and 4. [Why it matters] The backbeat on 2 and 4 makes melody phrases sit against a steady pulse and creates the push-pull feel in hybrid rhythm-and-lead parts. [How to practice] Use Fingerstyle — Travis Pinch Pattern as a warm-up to feel the pinch on beat 1, then play C for four bars with the thumb on beats 1 and 3 and index on beat 2 and middle on beat 4. Count aloud "1 2 3 4" and keep the thumb unmoving while the fingers pluck the backbeat notes.
sample.successCriteria: You can hold quarter-note thumb pulses on beats 1 and 3 while playing single treble-note answers on beats 2 and 4 for eight bars in a row at 80 BPM with every finger attack aligned to the counted beat.

sample.title: Snapped treble attacks
sample.summary: Pull the B and high E strings outward, then release them against the frets above a steady thumb bass.
sample.description: [What it is] Pulling the B and high E strings outward and releasing them so they snap against the frets while the thumb maintains a steady bass. [Why it matters] The outward snap creates the sharp, percussive treble attack Knopfler uses to make melody notes cut through a clean rhythm part. [How to practice] Warm up with Hybrid Picking — Chicken Pickin' to drill the outward pull and release motion. Then play a 2-bar G–Em loop with the thumb alternating on the low E and A strings while you snap the B string on the "&" of 2 and the high E on the "&" of 4 at 75 BPM, listening for a quick high-frequency attack and immediate damping after each snap.
sample.successCriteria: You can snap the B string on the "&" of 2 and the high E on the "&" of 4 over a steady alternating thumb for eight consecutive 2-bar loops at 75 BPM with each snap audible and the note stopped within one beat.

sample.title: Thumb, index, middle roles
sample.summary: Assign bass strings to the thumb and treble strings to index and middle across short chord-and-melody loops.
sample.description: [What it is] Assigning the low bass strings to the thumb and the B and high E strings to the index and middle fingers while you play short chord-and-melody loops. [Why it matters] A steady thumb bass frees the fingers to place melody and fills without losing the pulse, which is the backbone of Knopfler-style fingerstyle. [How to practice] Warm up with Fingerstyle — Alternating Thumb and feel the thumb rock between two bass strings on every beat over C, G and A minor. Then play a two-bar loop C–G with the thumb on the A and low E strings on beats 1 and 3 and index+middle filling beats 2 and 4 with single-note melodies on B and high E. Repeat at 70 BPM, keeping the thumb steady while you alter the treble notes each loop.
sample.successCriteria: You hold a steady alternating-thumb pulse on two bass strings while playing changing treble melodies on B and high E for four consecutive 2-bar loops at 70 BPM without the thumb missing a beat.
